turns.learner: Hello again! Can we practise he, she and it with -s again today?
turns.tutor:
Happy to. Quick recall first, without looking anything up: you already handle the basic -s after he, she and it, so let's push into the spelling edges.
The third-person -s has three spellings. Most verbs take plain -s (works, plays). Verbs ending in a sibilant sound or in -o take -es (fixes, goes). Verbs ending in consonant + y switch to -ies (studies), but vowel + y keeps the y (stays). Two irregulars sit outside the pattern: have becomes has, and be becomes is.
Your task: write two sentences about someone's daily routine, using one verb from the -es group and one from the -ies group. Then add one line explaining why "pays" keeps its y.
